description: Growing up in Vietnam, we have witnessed firsthand the devastating impacts of monsoon floods and typhoons across the Central region—where dense canopies often conceal submerged communities from optical satellites. When NASA opened the challenge, we saw an opportunity to bridge theoretical quantum information science with real-world disaster relief.
summary: FloodFusion-Q is an interactive web-based platform designed to visualize and analyze flood conditions before, during, and after storms. Focusing on Typhoon Maysak in Hanoi, Vietnam, the project primarily uses NASA NISAR GCOV and Digital Elevation Models (DEM) to identify potentially flooded areas and analyze terrain characteristics. Its key innovation is the integration of quantum-inspired computational methods to support satellite data analysis and surface change detection. The platform also combines additional datasets, including GUNW, IMERG, MERRA-2, SMAP, and SWOT RiverSP, to provide a broader understanding of flood dynamics. Through an interactive web map, users can explore geographic areas, visualize different data layers, and compare changes over time. FloodFusion-Q supports citizens in understanding potential travel risks, scientists in investigating environmental changes, and government agencies and rescue teams in identifying areas requiring urgent assessment. By transforming complex and fragmented satellite datasets into accessible information, FloodFusion-Q aims to improve flood awareness, support scientific research, and enhance disaster preparedness and respond
details:
FloodFusion-Q is an interactive web-based platform that combines Earth observation data, satellite image processing, and quantum-inspired computational methods to support flood monitoring and land surface change analysis. The project focuses on examining flood conditions before, during, and after Typhoon Maysak in Hanoi, Vietnam, with the goal of transforming complex satellite datasets into accessible, interactive, and meaningful geographic information.
Github: huyminhgithub/NASA-Space-App-Challenge-2026

The platform primarily uses NASA NISAR GCOV (Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance) and Digital Elevation Models (DEM). GCOV provides Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) backscatter measurements that support the identification of potential flooded areas and surface changes, even under cloudy or low-light conditions. DEM provides elevation information to identify low-lying areas, examine terrain characteristics, and support flood-risk assessment.

FloodFusion-Q also aims to integrate complementary datasets, including NISAR GUNW for ground displacement analysis, IMERG for precipitation monitoring, MERRA-2 for atmospheric conditions, SMAP and SME2 for soil moisture, SWOT RiverSP for river observations, and GPW v4 for population distribution.

How the System Works

FloodFusion-Q follows an integrated satellite-data processing and visualization workflow.

The system accesses Earth observation products through NASA Earthdata and specialized data repositories, including ASF, PO.DAAC, NSIDC, and GES DISC. It supports multiple geospatial formats, including HDF5, NetCDF, GeoTIFF, Shapefile, GeoPackage, and GeoJSON.

Satellite datasets are processed through geographic alignment, quality checks, spatial selection, and temporal organization before being converted into visualization-ready map layers.

A key research component is GCOV-QI-CD (Quantum-Information-Inspired Change Detection), a proposed unsupervised method for analyzing dual-polarimetric SAR observations. The algorithm represents the normalized backscatter power ratios of two polarization channels using a two-level density matrix inspired by quantum information theory. Quantum Jensen–Shannon Divergence (QJSD) is then used to measure changes in polarization composition between two observation times and calculates changes in total radar backscatter power using a logarithmic ratio, allowing it to detect intensity variations that may be overlooked when normalizing polarization components. The resulting change indicators can be interpreted alongside DEM and other environmental datasets to investigate potential flooding. GCOV-QI-CD remains a proposed research method requiring experimental validation; its quantum-inspired formulation does not require quantum hardware or establish a quantum computational advantage.

Processed information is presented through an interactive web map, allowing users to select geographic regions, switch between satellite datasets, explore terrain in 2D and 3D, and compare observations across different periods.

Development Tools and Technology Stack

Programming Languages

  • Python: Satellite-data processing, scientific computing, and backend development.
  • JavaScript (ES Modules): Interactive maps and browser-based visualization.
  • HTML and CSS: Web interface and dashboard design.
  • JSON: Data configuration, metadata, and API communication.

Frameworks and Visualization

  • FastAPI and Uvicorn: Backend services and data APIs.
  • Leaflet 1.9.4: Interactive 2D satellite maps and geographic overlays.
  • Three.js 0.160.0: 3D terrain visualization.
  • HTML Canvas: Raster image rendering.
  • Matplotlib and Folium: Scientific plots and geographic visualization.

Scientific and Geospatial Libraries

  • NumPy and SciPy: Numerical and scientific computing.
  • Rasterio, GeoPandas, Shapely, and PyProj: Raster processing, geographic analysis, and coordinate transformations.
  • h5py and netCDF4: Reading satellite datasets in HDF5 and NetCDF formats.
  • Pandas: Data organization and time-series analysis.
  • Pillow: Image processing and visualization.

Data Infrastructure

  • NASA Earthdata: Primary satellite-data discovery and access platform.
  • ASF, PO.DAAC, NSIDC, and GES DISC: Specialized NASA data repositories.
  • Copernicus DEM: Terrain elevation data.

Benefits

  • Flood Monitoring: Helps identify potentially flooded areas and observe surface changes using SAR imagery.
  • Terrain Analysis: Combines radar observations with elevation data to investigate low-lying regions and flood-prone terrain.
  • Quantum-Inspired Analysis: Explores information-theoretic approaches for unsupervised SAR change detection.
  • Multi-Source Integration: Brings together radar, rainfall, atmospheric, soil moisture, river, and population datasets.
  • Interactive Visualization: Provides accessible 2D and 3D maps with geographic selection and temporal comparisons.
  • Scientific Research Support: Enables researchers to explore satellite observations and identify areas requiring further investigation.
  • Disaster Preparedness: Supports preliminary identification of flood-affected regions for situational awareness and response planning.

Creativity and Innovation

FloodFusion-Q introduces a research-oriented approach to flood analysis by combining quantum-inspired SAR change detection with terrain-based geographic interpretation.

Its proposed GCOV-QI-CD method uses mathematical concepts from quantum information theory to examine changes in dual-polarimetric radar observations. By considering both polarization composition and backscatter intensity, the method aims to provide complementary indicators of surface change.

The platform's innovation also lies in integrating multiple Earth observation datasets within a unified interactive web map. Instead of requiring users to work with separate scientific tools and complex satellite files, FloodFusion-Q aims to make environmental information easier to explore and interpret.

This approach connects advanced remote-sensing research with practical geographic visualization while maintaining a focus on scientific transparency and reproducibility.

Intended Impact

FloodFusion-Q addresses a significant challenge in disaster monitoring: although satellite data is increasingly available, converting complex Earth observations into accessible and actionable flood information remains difficult.

The platform is designed for three primary user groups:

  • Citizens: Explore potentially flooded areas to better understand travel-related risks, alongside official road and safety information.
  • Scientists and Researchers: Investigate terrain characteristics, SAR observations, and surface changes more efficiently.
  • Government Agencies and Rescue Teams: Identify potentially affected regions and support the prioritization of field assessments and emergency-response planning.

In the long term, FloodFusion-Q aims to evolve into a scalable Earth observation analysis platform that combines satellite data, quantum-inspired research, and interactive mapping to support flood awareness, scientific investigation, and disaster preparedness.

In Conclusion

FloodFusion-Q bridges the gap between complex satellite observations and practical flood information. By integrating NISAR GCOV, DEM, complementary Earth observation datasets, and quantum-inspired analysis, the project aims to make flood monitoring more accessible, understandable, and useful.

Its ultimate goal is to help communities, researchers, and disaster-response organizations better understand flood-related changes and make informed decisions before, during, and after extreme weather events.
